provenance.source: NVIDIA HGX B200 datasheet (8-GPU baseboard, HBM3e)
provenance.notes: 192 GB HBM3e nominal per datasheet. Practical figures: ~186 GB shown on detailed datasheet entries, ~180 GB usable in cloud consoles (vendor-overhead). Keep the nominal figure as the canonical value; the 186/180 deltas are documentation/usable-overhead nuances, not separate SKUs.

provenance.source: NVIDIA HGX B200 datasheet (per-GPU HBM3e bandwidth, confirmed directly — not derived).
NVIDIA HGX B200 datasheet (per-GPU FP4 Tensor Core).
provenance.notes: 9 PFLOPS dense / 18 PFLOPS sparse per GPU. The widely-quoted marketing figure '20 PFLOPS FP4' is the sparse 2:1 number — keep dense/sparse distinction explicit when comparing across vendors.

provenance.source: NVIDIA HGX B200 datasheet individual-GPU column read at ~9 PFLOPS FP8 dense.
provenance.notes: Datasheet column read — confirm dense/sparse attribution before promoting to cited. NOTE: the prior value (4.5 PFLOPS) was the FP16/BF16 figure, mislabeled as FP8; corrected.

range.unit: GB HBM3e per Blackwell GPU (superchip = 2 GPUs, ~384 GB combined)

provenance.source: NVIDIA GB200 superchip positioning — Grace CPU + 2x Blackwell B200 GPUs interconnected via NVLink-C2C. Per-GPU HBM3e inherits from the standalone B200 datasheet (192 GB nominal).
provenance.notes: Per-GPU figure inherits from standalone B200 (192 GB HBM3e nominal); per-superchip aggregate is 2x that. Verify per-GPU vs per-superchip framing against the GB200 datasheet before promoting to cited.

provenance.source: NVIDIA GB200 per-GPU HBM3e bandwidth inherits from the B200 datasheet (8 TB/s).
provenance.notes: Per-GPU; the GB200 superchip adds NVLink-C2C bandwidth between Grace CPU and Blackwell GPUs that is separate from HBM bandwidth. Verify against the GB200 datasheet before promoting to cited.

provenance.source: NVIDIA GB200 per-GPU FP4 dense throughput inherits from the B200 datasheet (9 PFLOPS dense / 18 PFLOPS sparse per GPU).
provenance.notes: Per-GPU dense; sparse is 2x. Per-superchip total is ~18 PFLOPS dense across 2 Blackwell GPUs. Verify against the GB200 datasheet before promoting to cited.

provenance.source: NVIDIA HGX product page: HGX B300 8-GPU = 2.1 TB total ÷ 8 = 262.5 GB/GPU.
provenance.notes: Memory type not explicit on HGX page; likely HBM3e but unverified. Non-round figure (262.5) is unusual — verify against B300 datasheet.

protocol.text: Ethernet (Spectrum-4 ASIC) — AI-optimized merchant-Ethernet; NVIDIA's Ethernet track

provenance.source: NVIDIA Spectrum SN5600 datasheet — Spectrum-4 silicon, 64 OSFP 800GbE ports, 51.2 Tb/s total switch capacity.
NVIDIA Spectrum SN5600 datasheet — 64 OSFP 800GbE ports, 51.2 Tb/s total switch throughput, Spectrum-4 silicon. SN5600 is the canonical Spectrum-X switch.
provenance.notes: Promoted from directional/verify-needed to cited in phase 3c-1a — SN5600 datasheet (Spectrum-X platform's flagship 800 GbE switch) confirms the 800 Gbps per-port figure as a structured product spec, parallel to how Cornelis CN5000 throughput is treated.

provenance.source: NVIDIA does not publish a single Spectrum-X latency number publicly; positioning is sub-microsecond AI fabric.
provenance.notes: Directional band only. NVIDIA's strength is collective performance at scale, not raw per-hop latency.

provenance.source: NVIDIA does not publish a single message-rate number publicly for Spectrum-X.
provenance.notes: Directional band reflects Spectrum-X's positioning for high-throughput AI workloads.

scale_conditional.small_scale: parity (no decisive advantage at small node counts)
scale_conditional.large_scale: NVIDIA wins via SHARP / NCCL — in-network compute collapses AllReduce overhead at scale
scale_conditional.breakpoint: advantage emerges as cluster scales beyond ~64-128 nodes; SHARP / NCCL gap widens with node count

provenance.source: NVIDIA SHARP (Scalable Hierarchical Aggregation and Reduction Protocol) documentation; NCCL collective communication library public docs.
provenance.notes: Scale-conditional outcome — direction of effect is cited; breakpoint estimate is directional.

provenance.source: Analyst coverage (SemiAnalysis, IDC) consistently characterizes NVIDIA integrated networking as premium-priced vs disaggregated Ethernet.
provenance.notes: Directional band only. No published per-port CapEx number from NVIDIA.

provenance.source: Characterization synthesized from NVIDIA's positioning of Spectrum-X + Quantum-X800 as the integrated NVIDIA stack option.
provenance.notes: Customer-archetype framing, not a measured number.

protocol.text: InfiniBand (Quantum-3 ASIC) — distinct protocol from Spectrum-X's Ethernet; NVIDIA's InfiniBand track

provenance.source: NVIDIA Quantum-X800 (Q3400) product positioning — Quantum-3 InfiniBand ASIC, 200G-per-lane SerDes.

range.unit: Gbps per port (144 ports per switch — Q3400)

provenance.source: NVIDIA Quantum-X800 (Q3400) InfiniBand datasheet — 144 ports × 800 Gb/s per port, Quantum-3 ASIC, 200G-per-lane SerDes.
provenance.notes: Promoted from directional/verify-needed → cited in phase 3c-1b Quantum-X800 deepening. 144×800 per switch confirms the structural product nameplate spec, parallel to how Spectrum-X SN5600 is cited.

fabric_collective_op.text: SHARP v4 in-network computing — hardware collective-op acceleration (AllReduce, Reduce, etc. executed in the switch fabric)

provenance.source: NVIDIA Quantum-X800 product materials confirm SHARP v4 capability; SHARP (Scalable Hierarchical Aggregation and Reduction Protocol) is documented in NVIDIA networking docs.
provenance.notes: CAPABILITY is cited (Quantum-X800 supports SHARP v4). MAGNITUDE of acceleration (how much it speeds up collectives in a given workload) is workload-dependent and remains DIRECTIONAL — NVIDIA does not publish a single quantified speedup figure; do not assert a magnitude as cited.

fabric_buying_philosophy.text: integration — InfiniBand track: highest-performance NVIDIA fabric for trillion-param training, SHARP v4 in-network compute

provenance.source: NVIDIA's two-track fabric strategy: Spectrum-X (Ethernet) for AI-native scale-out + Quantum-X800 (InfiniBand) for tightly-coupled training. Both NVIDIA-integrated; protocol choice is the buyer-archetype split.
provenance.notes: Customer-archetype framing. Quantum-X800 buyers prioritize collective-op performance and SHARP in-network compute over Ethernet's ecosystem fit; distinct from Spectrum-X's Ethernet integration story but both are NVIDIA-integrated.
